subject: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA plan for private endpoints
messages:
From: Robert Lang <infra@acme-retail.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA for private endpoints

Laura / Priyom —

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. Attached is our latest network diagram (network-diagram-v2.pdf) and a short worksheet with our current cert inventory. Two immediate asks from our infra/security teams:

1) Where should TLS terminate for traffic from customer-facing apps into the private Redwood control plane (ALB / edge proxy / k8s ingress)? We prefer to avoid internet-exposed certs, but we need low-latency and simple rotation.

2) For internal-only endpoints (private.example.internal), what is the recommended certificate strategy? Do you support an internal CA / automated rotation (ideally integrated with our Vault/HSM)?

High-level constraints:
- We run on VPC with split-horizon DNS; private zone is not resolvable from internet.
- We store keys in a Vault cluster behind HSM and have strict export controls.
- Compliance requires a rotation window <= 90 days for leaf certs, and auditable rotation logs.

Can you sketch your recommended approach and any gotchas for our network team?

Thanks,
Robert Lang
Senior Infra Engineer, Acme Retail
infra@acme-retail.com

Attachment: network-diagram-v2.pdf (pdf)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Robert Lang <infra@acme-retail.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA for private endpoints

Thanks Robert — good context and helpful diagram. Looping in Priyom (platform lead) and Mina (security) to make sure we cover operational and compliance constraints. High-level recommendations up front:

- Termination point: prefer terminating TLS at the on-prem edge proxy (Envoy/HAProxy) that sits in your DMZ/VPC edge. Rationale: preserves end-to-end TLS to our pods if you require mutual TLS, avoids exposing private certs to public ALBs, and gives you central control of ingress TLS policies.

- Internal CA: recommend issuing internal leaf certs from your Vault-backed PKI. Redwood supports trust establishment via an uploaded root/intermediate (we keep only the public certs). We can integrate with cert-manager-style agents to automate renewals from your Vault PKI or accept signed CSR bundles if you prefer to keep signing strictly within your HSM.

- Rotation: 60–90 day TTL for leaf certs with automated renewal. For private endpoints we recommend 60 days if you plan aggressive key rotation; 90 days is acceptable if you have automated tooling and strong audit logs.

- Split-horizon DNS: keep private endpoints (private.example.internal) in your private hosted zone. Redwood’s control plane will resolve to private IPs when configured with your VPC peering / routing. Avoid exposing CNAMEs into public DNS.

- mTLS: recommend mTLS between the edge proxy and Redwood service frontends if you need strong mutual auth. We can provide the client certs and trust bundle to your proxy, or consume certs you issue.

Action items:
1) Priyom — please confirm whether you prefer Redwood to pull certs via an agent (cert-manager style) or accept pre-signed bundles.
2) Robert — please confirm HSM constraints (can you export public-only intermediate certs? do signing operations have an API we can call?).
3) Mina — we’ll need your checklist for auditable rotations (key wrapping, rotation events).

Happy to sketch a sample Envoy TLS/mTLS config for your edge proxy once we pick the pattern.

—Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Robert Lang <infra@acme-retail.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA for private endpoints

Robert / Laura — quick technical follow-up from platform side (copying Hiro for infra details):

Option A — Terminate at edge proxy (recommended):
- Edge proxy handles TLS + (optionally) mTLS. Proxy forwards to Redwood via private peering over TLS, either re-terminating or using mTLS to Redwood frontends.
- Benefits: central point for DDoS, WAF, rate-limiting, and certificate control.
- Ops: we’d ask you to run a small agent (k8s DaemonSet or standalone binary) that can fetch certs from Vault and place them into the proxy hot-reload path. Redwood can provide an example cert-manager controller that speaks to Vault (does not require private keys to leave HSM if you prefer CSR flow).

Option B — Terminate at Redwood ingress within your VPC (less preferred):
- Requires exposing an internal load balancer + private DNS. Simpler cert management on Redwood side, but you give up central control at your edge and add network complexity.

Cert specifics:
- We support RSA 2048 and ECDSA P-256 for leaf certs.
- For internal CA model: upload a PEM chain (root + intermediates) to the Redwood control plane so we can trust certs presented by your proxy. Private keys should never be uploaded.
- Rotation automation: recommend cert-manager (ACME not needed) + Vault PKI. We’ll provide sample helm values for cert-manager + Vault agent. TTL: 60 days recommended; renew at 45 days.

Network notes:
- Ensure split-horizon returns internal A records for *.redwood.private pointing at your peered endpoints.
- On routing: allow TCP/HTTPS from the proxy to Redwood control-plane IP ranges (I’ll share exact CIDRs).

If that sounds good we’ll produce the sample Envoy config and a cert-manager + Vault deployment manifest (no private keys).

—Priyom
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Robert Lang <infra@acme-retail.com>
Cc: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA for private endpoints

Robert / team — a few security items we need to validate before we sign off on the design:

1) Key custody and HSM: must confirm that private signing keys never leave your HSM. If you prefer Redwood-managed rotation, keys must be generated in an HSM-backed KMS and we require an API for signing or an exported intermediate public cert.

2) Audit/rotation logs: rotation events (renewal time, operator, runbook id) need to be exported to an audit log (S3 or your SIEM). We need a retention policy for at least 1 year for rotation artifacts.

3) Trust store management: when you upload intermediates to Redwood, we need a documented procedure for replacing trust bundles with at least a 7-day overlap to avoid outages.

4) mTLS vs TLS-only: if you enable mTLS, please provide the expected client identity format (CN/SAN) and whether you plan to rotate client certs on the same cadence as server certs. mTLS reduces risk but increases ops overhead.

Please confirm these points. Once confirmed, we’ll provide the compliance checklist and an example Envoy config that satisfies our audit logging requirements.

—Mina (Security Engineering)

From: Robert Lang <infra@acme-retail.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>, DataTrust SG <security@datatrust.example>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem TLS termination + internal CA for private endpoints

Laura / team — thanks, this is very helpful. Quick answers and next steps: 

- HSM: we will not export private keys. We can issue CSRs to our HSM-backed CA via a signing API (Vault PKI with HSM HSM plugin). We can provide an intermediate public cert for you to trust.
- Audit logs: Vault already writes audit logs to our SIEM (retained 2 years). We can share a filtered view for rotation events.
- Trust bundle rotation: we will follow the 7-day overlap rollout.
- mTLS: we want mTLS between edge proxy and Redwood frontends. Client cert CN will be of the form cn=acme-proxy-<region> and we will rotate clients every 90 days.

Next steps: can Redwood produce — by EOD Wednesday — an Envoy example for TLS termination + client mTLS validation (include hot-reload hints for cert updates), and a stub cert-manager + Vault manifest that demonstrates automated renewals (no private keys in repo)? Also sending over our cert-rotation worksheet (cert-rotation-proposal.xlsx) for reference.

If you can include a short rollout plan for a canary (one region first) that would be ideal.

Best,
Robert
Senior Infra Engineer, Acme Retail

Attachments: cert-rotation-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
